 Order

The petitioners - accused Nos.13 to 15 and other accused have been charge sheeted for the offences under Sections 34, 420 of IPC alleging that, the registered agreement of sale was executed in favour of the defacto complainant after receiving the advance sale consideration of Rs.1,00,000/- out of total sale consideration of Rs.3,50,000/-, and when the time specified for execution of the sale deed was coming to an end, the accused Nos.1 to 11 with one or the other pretext postponed to execute the sale deed, and thereafter colluding with other accused created the sale deed conveying the subject property by describing the property as Sy.No.121/2.
The cognizance taken by the learned Magistrate is impugned in this petition.

2. The learned counsel for the petitioners submits that, in the absence of any allegation that, the petitioners - accused herein at the time of execution of registration of agreement of sale had a dishonest intention to cheat the defacto complainant, the cognizance taken by the learned Magistrate is impermissible.

3. The learned counsel for the respondent No.1 submits that, the petitioners - accused Nos.13 to 15 herein by conniving with accused Nos.1 to 11 have created the sale deed purportedly showing the survey number as 121/2 with an intention to cheat the respondent No.1.

sentences.text: 4. I have considered the submission of the learned counsel appearing for the parties.

5. There must be a specific allegation or material that, there was dishonest intention on the part of the petitioners - accused Nos.13 to 15 herein from the date of registration of agreement of sale to cheat the defacto complainant, which is sine quo non to hold the accused guilty of the commission of the offence under Section 420 of IPC.

In the instant case, there is no allegation that, the petitioner - accused No.13 herein, who is the purchaser of the subject property, and accused Nos.14 and 15, who are the witnesses to the sale deed, had dishonest intention to cheat the defacto complainant at the time of execution of agreement of sale in favour the defacto complainant.
The petitioners had no role in execution of the agreement of sale in favour of the defacto complainant.
In the absence of essential ingredients so as to constitute the commission of offence under Section 420 of IPC, the cognizance taken by the learned Magistrate is impermissible.

Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER i) Criminal petition is allowed.
ii) The impugned proceedings in CC No.154/2016 pending on the file of the Prl. Civil Jduge (Jr.Dn.) and JMFC Court, Gubbi, insofar as it relates to the petitioner - accused Nos.13 to 15 is hereby quashed.
iii) The Trial Court to dispose of the suit in OS No.288/2015 filed by the defacto complainant for specific performance of agreement of sale and also for cancellation of sale deed executed in favour of accused No.13 without being influenced by the observation made in this order.
